title: ABT — Pilot List management and validation
preface: This test is to confirm the cEMV Pilot List can be distributed to a PV via TMS and that EMV cards are validated per their pilot-list membership.
preconds:
**GIVEN** a Glider PV with cEMV is configured via TMS with Enable Pilot List=True and Enable Registration Mode=False, and the binary pilot list (pilotlist.dat) imported into the Pilot List File field
**AND** you have an EMV card on the list and one not on the list
**AND** you can verify records in the CloudFare activity log

steps.content: **WHEN** the pilot list dataset is deployed to the PV via TMS
steps.expected: **THEN** the PV applies the pilot list configuration

steps.content: **WHEN** you present an EMV card that is on the Pilot List, then one that is not
steps.expected:
**THEN** the on-list card is accepted per the pilot rules
**AND** the not-on-list card is rejected with the standard rejection screen
**THEN** the outcomes are recorded in the CloudFare activity log

citations: FBD-100720 §3-4 (Pilot List Creation/Distribution): 'Enable Registration Mode' and 'Enable Pilot List' are mutually exclusive dataset settings (True/False vs False/True) — a device cannot have both applied at once, so the original 'apply pilot list including registration mode' precondition was self-contradictory
FBD-100720 §3: the distributed list is the binary pilotlist.dat imported into the TMS 'Pilot List File' field, not a 'pilotlist.zip' applied to the device
FBD-100720 §4 para 330: 'If the FEIG token is not on the list then the device will reject the tap with the standard rejection screen'

FBD-100720 §3: the CSV<->binary conversion is done by the back-office 'Pilot List Converter' tool run by Arrive personnel, not a device/TMS export step; the registration file (from a device in Registration Mode) uploads as a zip to CloudFare's Device Logging service, separately from Pilot List distribution
change_note: CORRECTED per coherence-audit pv.findings.md (Med finding, 2026-07-17), now verified against the full FBD-100720 text. Three fixes: (1) registration mode and pilot-list mode are mutually exclusive TMS dataset settings, so the case can no longer claim both apply at once — narrowed to the pilot-list-validation dataset only (registration-mode data capture is a separate scenario, out of scope for this case); (2) fixed artefact names — pilotlist.dat (binary) into the 'Pilot List File' field, not 'pilotlist.zip'; (3) dropped the garbled step 3 'CSV to DAT, download as CSV from Device Log Manager' claim — the CSV<->binary round-trip is a back-office Pilot List Converter tool step (not a device/TMS action), and the artefact that actually zips/uploads to CloudFare Device Logging is the *registration* file, a different flow this case no longer asserts. Not-on-list outcome is now grounded on FBD-100720 para 330's exact wording ('standard rejection screen') instead of the vaguer 'not-included rule'.

preconds:
**GIVEN** a Glider PV with cEMV is showing the Present screen
**AND** you have cards for each decline condition (card not read, unsupported scheme e.g. AMEX, expired, ODA fail, on BIN list, on Deny list)
**AND** a card can be re-presented within the configured ABT Passback window
**AND** you can verify records in the CloudFare activity log

steps.content: **WHEN** you present a card that hits one of those decline conditions
steps.expected: **THEN** the PV shows the Please Try Again outcome with the corresponding decline reason

steps.content: **WHEN** the route is "Tap On Only (Flat Fare)" or "Tap On Tap Off"
steps.expected: **THEN** cEMV taps are enabled for that route type

steps.content: **WHEN** no valid fare is found or the boarding location is outside the configured area
**WHEN** a card is re-presented within the configured ABT Passback window
steps.expected:
**THEN** the PV shows the Passback outcome, not a decline error
**AND** no second fare is taken for the re-presented card (pins TIBU-22322)

citations: TIBU-22322 (canonical cEMV-decline story, 7 conditions): card not read (no audit), unsupported scheme — only Visa/Mastercard/Maestro valid (no audit), expired (DeclinedReason 1), ODA fail (DeclinedReason 3), on BIN list (DeclinedReason 15), on Deny list (DeclinedReason 2), Passback (DeclinedReason 20) — 'invalid BIN'/'AID fail'/'card clash' from the original wording are not among these 7 and were not found in FBD-100389, FBD-100651 or FBD-100658 either
FBD-100651 §4.3.6-4.3.8 (BIN/Deny/Passback checks) — matches TIBU-22322's reasons 15/2/20 verbatim

FBD-100389 para 148: card scheme validity is itself checked 'based on the AID' — so 'AID fail' in the original wording was a redundant restatement of the unsupported-scheme condition, not a distinct decline reason

knowledge/flows/pv-flow-annotations.md (Technician Menu - Platform Validator flow, 24 screens/12 annotations): the enumerated Technician Menu pages are Location Settings, Software Versions, Brightness, Force Communications, Network Settings, Configuration Versions, Audio — no cEMV enable/disable toggle appears anywhere in the flow
change_note: CORRECTED per coherence-audit pv.findings.md (Low finding, 'confirm a Technician-Menu cEMV toggle exists; if not, drop that clause') and gap-register — now resolved directly from source rather than left open. (1) The decline-condition list is tightened to the exact 7 conditions in TIBU-22322/FBD-100651: 'invalid BIN' folded into 'on BIN list', 'AID fail' dropped as redundant with 'unsupported scheme' (FBD-100389 para 148 — both are AID-based scheme checks), and 'card clash' dropped entirely — it has zero hits across FBD-100389, FBD-100651, FBD-100658 or the TIBU-22322 decline-story and could not be grounded; drafting a new gap-register question rather than silently reinventing or silently deleting it (see final report). (2) Step 3's 'cEMV is disabled in the Technician Menu' clause is dropped — the full Technician Menu flow annotations enumerate every page and none exposes a cEMV toggle, confirming the prior audit's suspicion; no-fare/out-of-area disablement (already asserted, and already the subject of dedicated case C4101001) stands on its own.

preface: This test is to confirm the FEIG reader reads Translink DESFire smartcards and accepts valid / rejects invalid EMV taps.
preconds:
**GIVEN** a Glider PV with a FEIG reader is in service
**AND** you have a DESFire smartcard, a valid EMV card and an invalid EMV card
**AND** you can verify records in the CloudFare activity log and MERIT

steps.expected: **THEN** the FEIG reads and validates the smartcard

steps.content: **WHEN** you tap the valid EMV card, then the invalid EMV card
steps.expected:
**THEN** the valid EMV tap is accepted
**AND** the invalid one is rejected with the reason
**THEN** the taps are recorded in the CloudFare activity log and MERIT

citations: FBD-100236 'Translink DESFire ABT Card Format Specification' v6.00: the Translink PV smartcard is a DESFire EV3 card (§3); zero mentions of ITSO anywhere in the spec
change_note: CORRECTED — cross-surface/terminology error found during this audit: the case called the smartcard an 'ITSO smartcard'. ITSO is a different, unrelated UK smartcard ticketing standard; Translink's own card-format spec (FBD-100236) is explicitly titled and scoped to the DESFire EV3 format, with no ITSO reference anywhere in the document. This looks like boilerplate carried over from a generic/other-operator PV test template. Corrected to 'DESFire smartcard' throughout; the FEIG-reads-a-non-EMV-smartcard behaviour itself is otherwise unchanged and not in question.

change_note: COHERENCE FIX (spot-check finding): re-verified this case's citation against pv-failover-restore.rewrite.json / .changelog.md — the restored title/preface/preconds/steps hold up (grounded on REQ-2746.0 + TIBU-24428, matches Jira). But the case's top-level Expected-result field was never updated by that restore (the restore rewrite only supplied title/preface/preconds/steps) and still reads the pre-restore generic wording ('keeps validating with comms interrupted/lost... fails over to the secondary channel'), which doesn't name the Ethernet->cellular direction, the PrimaryCommsChannelFailed/812 event, or the fail-back leg the steps now assert. Corrected to summarise the actual (restored) step content. No behavioural change — title/preface/preconds/steps unchanged from the applied restore.

steps.content: **WHEN** the passenger taps on for a journey
steps.expected: **THEN** the PV records a flat-fare journey (ABT Tag successful)

steps.content: **WHEN** the same card taps again immediately after (same reader), and taps multiple times across the day
steps.expected:
**THEN** the immediate re-tap is declined as Passback, not charged as a second fare
**AND** the day's taps are aggregated under the applicable capping rule

steps.content: **WHEN** you check the back office for the journeys
steps.expected: **THEN** the flat-fare journey appears in the CloudFare activity log and MERIT

citations: FBD-100651 §4.3.8 Passback Check: a card re-tapped within the configured ABT Passback window is declined (DeclinedReason 20), not charged again
FBD-100651 para 295: Glider taps are aggregated according to the applicable capping rule (either a separate Glider rule, or combined with the existing Metro rule)
change_note: CORRECTED — step 2's original wording bundled two different mechanisms under one vague label ('daily-tap rules... the immediate re-tap is treated as passback') without an outcome for the 'taps multiple times across the day' half of the WHEN. Reworded so each half of the claim has a grounded, matching THEN: the immediate same-reader re-tap is the Passback check (FBD-100651 §4.3.8, correctly a decline not a duplicate charge); repeated taps across the day are governed by the capping rule (FBD-100651 para 295) — renamed from the ungrounded 'daily-tap rules' term. No cap value is asserted, per the configured-value convention (gap-register Q14).
